_comment: Registers agentgateway in the platform catalog. Apply with:
cortexctl create -f platform-services/agentgateway/register.json
This runs agentgateway in STANDALONE mode — a single binary that serves its
own UI. Upstream also ships a Kubernetes mode built on the Gateway API, with
a controller and four CRDs. That mode is not used here, and NOTES.md records
why: three of those CRDs are larger than the annotation Argo writes when it
applies a resource, so they cannot be installed through the platform as it
is configured today.
No infrastructure is declared. Standalone agentgateway keeps its
configuration in a file and needs no database, cache or object store. It
gains dependencies only when something is configured that has them — a
global rate limit needs Redis, for instance — so there is nothing to
provision until then.
No roles are declared either. agentgateway has no role vocabulary of its
own, so the platform grants the default 'user' role and access is simply
whether you may reach it at all.
authRequired puts it behind the platform's login. The Entra redirect URI is
NOT automated: add https://agentgateway.apps.msft.ae/oauth2/callback to app
6eb003c0-169c-4b12-bc5e-aa5d6af04f2b by hand, or sign-in fails with a
redirect-mismatch error that says nothing about this file.
exposeService must match the Service the chart actually creates. This
chart's fullname helper collapses to the chart name, so it is
'agentgateway'. Guessing wrong gives a gateway 500 with healthy pods.

applications.name: agentgateway
applications.description: One gateway for LLM, MCP and agent-to-agent traffic, with routing, policy, cost controls and an admin UI.
